title: Incident closure: Aug 28 service blip — readout, timeline, and verification request
text:
Incident closure: Aug 28 service blip — readout, timeline, and verification request

['From: Alicia Moreno <alicia@claritybank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Service blip on Aug 28th — request for timeline and fixes

Hannah / David,

Thanks again for the quick support during the Aug 28th blip. Our internal compliance team has requested a concise timeline and what you believe the root cause was. Specifically:
- Precise event timeline (first anomaly, mitigation steps, full recovery)
- Root cause expressed in customer-facing terms
- Actions you will take to reduce recurrence and expected completion dates
- Any data/evidence we can include in our audit package

We need that by next Friday (9/12) if possible — our audit window opens the week after.

Appreciate the transparency.

Thanks,
Alicia Moreno
Director, Platform Ops — Clarity Bank

", "From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Moreno <alicia@claritybank.com>
Date: 2025-09-04T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Service blip on Aug 28th — request for timeline and fixes

Hannah / Neha — quick internal note before we finalize the packet for Alicia. (Quoted original below.)

Summary of technical findings (short bullets for customer):
- What happened: Between 14:12 and 14:37 UTC on Aug 28 ingestion of long-running batched requests caused a KV-cache eviction cascade on a subset of inference nodes that increased tail latency above SLO for ~25% of requests.
- Why it happened: A combination of an edge-case batching pattern (long prefixes + variable sequence length) and an under-provisioned kernel selector led to repeated cache evictions during a short spike. This caused additional token re-computation, increasing latency and momentarily exhausting the request queue on affected workers.
- Immediate mitigation: We throttled request concurrency and moved traffic to warm standby nodes; automated cache warm-up reduced re-computation in 25 minutes.

Customer-facing action items (owner, ETA):
1) Kernel selector fix — add safeguards to avoid downselecting heavy kernels when sequence-length variance high (D. Kim, 2025-09-15).
2) Dynamic cache warm-up — pre-warm KV cache on scale events (Neha Kapoor, 2025-09-22).
3) Canary policy tweak — stricter latency checks during rollouts and automated fallback to compatible quantized variant (Hannah Schmitt, 2025-09-18).
4) Additional monitoring & alerts — new alert for repeated eviction patterns + runbook (SRE, 2025-09-08).

Evidence bundle we're preparing: aggregated event logs, worker-level traces for the affected window, and token-level latency histograms (attached CSV).

Recommend we ship a concise executive summary to Alicia and include the technical attachments and the verification plan (weekly checks for 60 days).

To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@claritybank.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-08T10:00:00Z
Subject: Incident closure: Aug 28 — technical summary, timeline, actions & verification

Alicia —

Attached is the final closure packet for the Aug 28th service blip. Thank you for your patience; below is a concise executive readout for your audit team, followed by the attachments and verification plan.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Impact: Short-lived latency increase on Aug 28 that affected ~25% of requests for 25 minutes; no data corruption or token loss.
- Root cause: A KV-cache eviction cascade triggered by a rare batching pattern combined with a suboptimal kernel selection path on a subset of workers.
- Resolution: Traffic moved to standby nodes and cache warm-up completed; normal service restored by 14:37 UTC.

Timeline (UTC)
- 14:12 — first elevated token latency detected by internal alerting (tail latency > 99th pct SLO).
- 14:14 — automated scaling triggered; canary nodes began receiving diverted traffic.
- 14:18 — repeated cache evictions observed on 3 worker pods; we initiated concurrency throttle for affected routes.
- 14:28 — warm-up completed on standby nodes; observed steady decline in tail latency.
- 14:37 — latency returned to SLO band; canary checks passed; normal routing resumed.

Root cause (customer language)
- During a short traffic surge, a specific request pattern caused cache entries to be evicted repeatedly on some workers. Evictions forced the system to recompute more tokens than usual, which degrades latency. A kernel-selection guard inadvertently allowed a heavier compute path to run under those request characteristics, amplifying the effect.

Corrective actions (owner — ETA)
- SRE: Immediate alert & runbook published for eviction cascades; ongoing (SRE team — 2025-09-08)
- Runtime: Kernel selector safeguards added to prevent heavy paths under high variance (David Kim — 2025-09-15)
- Runtime: Implement dynamic KV pre-warm on scale events (Neha Kapoor — 2025-09-22)
- Platform: Canary policy tightened; automated fallback to compatible quantized variant during anomalous latency (Hannah Schmitt — 2025-09-18)

Verification plan
- Evidence attached: clarity-rca-20250908.pdf (customer-ready RCA), event-timeline-aug28.csv (worker traces & histograms), evidence-log-aug28.txt (support logs).
- Shared dashboard: https://redwood.app/metrics/claritybank/incident-aug28 (read-only link).
- We propose weekly verification emails with lightweight snapshots for 8 weeks and a short wrap-up call at week 6 to confirm stability.

Next steps
- Please confirm receipt and let us know if you want a walkthrough call (30 minutes) this week.
- If your audit team needs additional raw artifacts (full trace bundles), we can provide them under an access agreement — indicate preferred format and a point of contact.

Attachments: clarity-rca-20250908.pdf (PDF), event-timeline-aug28.csv (CSV), evidence-log-aug28.txt (text)

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Also: our procurement team will review the SLA details and reach out separately if they need a formal credit request — I'll loop you in where necessary.
